title: Reverse Engineering Browser VM opcode workspace v2

sample_count.description: Sum of workspace sample_count values. Native Wasm observation and native guest sample counts are reported per workspace and are not included.

staticEvidenceClass.description: Static dispatch structure. A br_table or call_indirect site is never a proven guest ISA.

structuralEvidenceClass.description: Workspace claim. guest-opcode-isa requires samples with guest PC units or an exact-hash owned effect declaration.

segments.description: Producer 2.9.0 and later, element rows only: each active segment for this table with its evaluated placement, at most 64; omitted_segment_count counts the rest. placed segments fill real slots at offset; relative segments read an imported global, directly or through a defined global, and fill no listed slot; out-of-range segments end past the table's declared minimum and are not placed; unreached segments follow an out-of-range segment, so instantiation traps before applying them; unresolved offsets are outside the evaluated constant subset.

omitted_segment_count.description: Element rows only: active segments of this table beyond the 64 listed in segments.

sample_count.description: Accepted dispatch report or dispatch sample records for this handler. Native counts are separate fields; producer 2.7.0 and later never add them here.

native_wasm_sample_count.description: Accepted physical br_table executions at this exact site and arm. The same execution can also appear in native_guest_sample_count; never add the two.

native_guest_sample_count.description: Accepted native guest samples at this exact site and arm. The same execution can also appear in native_wasm_sample_count; never add the two.

sample_count.description: Accepted dispatch report or dispatch sample records, matching samples. Producer 2.7.0 and later exclude native Wasm observations and native guest samples; documents from earlier producers summed all three streams.

dispatch_classification.description: Producer 2.9.0 and later: the analysis result's structural dispatch classification for this artifact. Only interpreter-candidate sites can carry guest opcode claims.

native_wasm_observation_count.description: Accepted physical br_table executions. One execution at an adapter site also produces a native guest sample, so this count overlaps native_guest_sample_count.

native_guest_sample_count.description: Accepted native guest samples. Each one coincides with a physical br_table execution when the physical sampler is enabled, so this count overlaps native_wasm_observation_count.

monotonic_time_ns.description: Monotonic time of the accepted observation event, copied from the native event. Optional: documents written before this field remain valid.

nativeUint64.description: Canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal, 0 through 18446744073709551615; no sign or leading zeros.

nativeInt64.description: Canonical signed 64-bit decimal, -9223372036854775808 through 9223372036854775807; no plus sign, leading zeros, or negative zero.

monotonic_time_ns.description: Monotonic time of the accepted guest sample event, copied from the native event. Optional: documents written before this field remain valid.

nativeGuestSample.description: Native observation with explicit artifact and invocation bindings. Consumers additionally verify exact sites, artifact digests, PC arithmetic, snapshot bounds, default-arm selection and causal identities; schema validation alone is not evidence of guest semantics.

dispatchClassification.description: Analyzer interpretation of stored artifact bytes. Each site states how control picks the next handler, where the selector value comes from, and whether the dispatch repeats in a selector-advancing loop. confidence is always structural. It never rewrites captured evidence and never raises a VM tier. Lands as one unit with its first two producer commits; no released document predates it, so it keeps version 1.

site_count.description: Classified sites. Sites found but refused by a work bound are counted in omissions, not here.

omitted_site_count.description: Classified sites not listed: site_count minus the listed sites.

omissions.description: Classification work that a bound refused. Never silent: omitted_records counts dispatch sites found but not classified.

role.description: Derived from the record. interpreter-candidate: repeats=loop with cursor_index, cursor_pointer or frame_slot on switch_on_value, handler_table or compare_chain, unless buffer_kind is string or arguments, and unless the selector is a second-level lookup (through_lookup) on a switch or ladder; a handler table reads its handler through one lookup by design. multiplexer: repeats=once with call_argument on the same kinds; its arms or constants are routing labels and no guest opcode is claimed. other: everything else.

function_index.description: Wasm function index (imports first); null for JavaScript and module-level records.

function_body_offset.description: Wasm code entry offset, or JavaScript function region start.

byte_offset.description: Artifact byte offset of the dispatch instruction or first comparison.

line.description: JavaScript one-based line; null for Wasm.

column.description: JavaScript one-based character column; null for Wasm.

expression.description: Bounded rendering of the instructions or source expression that produced the selector. Inert text.

byte_offset.description: Offset of the closest producing write or load, when it is not the dispatch itself.

through_lookup.description: The selector is a table read keyed by a value loaded at a cursor, such as types[q[head++]], rather than the fetched value itself.

arm_count.description: br_table explicit arms, JavaScript case labels, comparisons in a ladder, type-matching table slots, or exported functions.

loop.description: The selector-advancing loop for repeats=loop, otherwise the innermost enclosing loop; null outside loops.

buffer_kind.description: JavaScript cursor buffers only. string or arguments marks a cursor loop over text or call arguments, which reads characters or argument values rather than opcodes.

matching_slots.description: Real table slot indexes, after evaluated element offsets, whose function signature equals the call's type. A prefix of at most 32. Null when the table layout is unknown.
